references.text: God hears Ishmael's cry, echoing the promise that the Lord has heard Hagar's distress (the meaning of the name Ishmael).
God confirms the promise concerning Ishmael and pledges to bless him and make him a great nation.
The angel of the Lord appears to a woman and announces that she will conceive and bear a son—a closely parallel motif to the angel's message to Hagar.
The angel tells Mary that she will conceive and bear a son and give him a name—the same pattern found in the angel's words to Hagar.
"This afflicted one cried out, and the Lord heard"—a thematic parallel to the Lord having heard Hagar's distress (ki-shama JHVH el-onyekh).
Ishmael's descendants and the fulfillment of the promise given to Hagar concerning her son.
Prophetic parallel: God's intervention in an impossible pregnancy and the naming that carries a theological core (God hears versus God is with us).
Literary and theological parallel: The angel of the Lord announces the birth of a special child to a woman in distress or barrenness.
Thematic connection: God's response to prayer and suffering by granting a son, announced by an angel.
Contrast in salvation history: Naming as a response to suffering (Ishmael) versus deliverance from sin (Jesus).
Prophetic parallel: Use of "Behold, ... shall bear a son" and naming as a theological sign.
Narrative parallel: God's double promise concerning sons (Ishmael and Isaac), each accompanied by a command to name them.
Theological parallel: Naming based on the expression "the Lord has heard" as an answer to suffering or prayer.
Strong thematic parallel: Naming as a direct response to "the Lord has heard" a woman's distress or neglect.
Prophetic parallel: The naming of a child who carries a prophetic message from God.
Strong thematic parallel: Naming in response to the fact that 'the Lord has seen/heard' a woman's distress.
Theological connection: Naming of a son based on a divine revelation.
Narrative parallel: God's promise to bless Ishmael and make him into a great nation.
Strong thematic parallel: Naming in response to the fact that 'God has heard' a woman's distress.
Theological parallel: Naming of a child who carries a prophetic message from God.
